title: Design: Choosing Imported in Status keeps the table headings in place
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, the asset's current owner.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, a payer.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer C, the asset's earlier owner.
  • Have a new asset for this test, asset 1, now owned by customer A, that earlier belonged to customer C, with work order 1 for customer C billing itself (made first, while customer C owned it) and work order 2 for customer A billed to customer B (made later), both at the test location.
  • Open the attached picture bt-p7-10-after-work-orders-tab-top.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_steps:
1. Open asset 1's Work Orders tab from customer A's page.
  2. Click the "Customer" filter chip.
  3. Tick customer C.
  4. Click outside the panel.
  5. Take a screenshot of the page.
  6. Add Imported to the Status filter.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 and work order 2 are listed, with a "Bill To" column.

Step 2:

  • The panel opens.

Step 3:

  • Customer C is ticked.

Step 4:

  • Only work order 1 is listed.
  • The "Bill To" column still shows, blank on work order 1.

Step 5:

  • You have a picture of where each heading, field and button sits before the change.

Step 6:

  • The "Customer" chip is disabled and reads "Customer: All customers".
  • Work order 1 and work order 2 are listed again.
  • The "Bill To" column shows customer B's name on work order 2.
  • Every column heading is in the same place as in your screenshot: none has moved left or right.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Bill To", Confluence 1003585538, version 0.5 (6 Nov 2026, pending approval, Chris Ward), read 9 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-12289, story SV-12316 (Story 14, Asset Work Orders tab: whole history and Customer filter)

  • S14-N1: “When the Status filter includes Imported, the Customer filter is disabled and cleared.”
  • S14-R6: “A "Bill To" column shows when at least one row bills someone else; it is blank on self-billed rows.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Bill To design" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2prSHgwt2tWCz96QD2DWkd), version 1794510417-a68d (its boards are byte-identical to version 1794239066-4906 read 9 Nov 2026), read 13 Nov 2026: pictures "Work Orders tab, top" (page 7 "Asset Work Orders tab", This build). Compare the screen with the pictures; the expected results come from the PRD.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • bt-p7-10-after-work-orders-tab-top.png

The design's own words:

  • “A "Bill To" column sits right after Customer because a loaded row bills someone else. S2-17579 reads "Buda Truck Repair", "Valders Diesel & Fleet Repair".”

The design draws no Imported state. These results follow the suggested answer of question 17 (the column is decided from the asset's list before any filter).
